# UHS Leaders Connect with Regional Business Community at The Forum of Executive Women’s Annual Leadership Event


default


default


**King of Prussia, PA (November 2, 2026)** – UHS leaders joined executives and business leaders from across the Greater Philadelphia region for The Forum of Executive Women’s Annual Leadership Breakfast, reinforcing the company’s longstanding commitment to leadership development, professional advancement and regional collaboration.


Representing UHS at The Forum of Executive Women Annual Leadership Event 2026 were (L to R) Roselle Charlier, Elizabeth Esteves, Yasmine Kamara, Regina Hampton, Diane Hill Lieb, Maria English and Meredith Clayton.


The annual gathering brings together more than 500 influential leaders from diverse industries to share perspectives, build meaningful connections and explore opportunities to advance business and community impact throughout the region. “Strong leadership is built through connection, shared perspectives and a commitment to continuous growth,” said Roselle Charlier, Vice President and Chief Marketing and Communications Officer at UHS. “Our longstanding relationship with The Forum of Executive Women reflects our belief in the power of collaboration and the importance of creating opportunities for leaders to learn from one another, inspire progress and make a meaningful difference in the communities we serve.”


UHS was once again recognized in The Forum’s annual Women in Leadership Report for its representation of women on the company’s Board of Directors, reflecting the organization’s commitment to bringing diverse perspectives and experiences to its leadership. Through its continued engagement with The Forum of Executive Women, UHS supports opportunities for professional development, meaningful dialogue and connections that strengthen both its organization and the broader Greater Philadelphia business community.


## About The Forum of Executive Women


Founded in 1977, The Forum of Executive Women is the Greater Philadelphia Region’s premier women’s organization, actively working to bring together, and leverage the influence of, professional women to expand the impact and power of women in the workplace and beyond. Forum membership has grown over four decades to comprise more than 600 of the most influential leaders throughout the region. Visit[foew.com](https://www.foew.com/) for more information.
